$comment: Hatsu's OWN workflow policy. This file is the policy half of the two-file configuration model documented in docs/WORKFLOW.md: nen/contract.json says what nen EXECUTES (lanes, argv, preconditions, hosts, targets), this file says what the workflow DECIDES with (branch shape, which declared verbs run per iteration, the coverage ladder, where reports go, which trailers a commit may carry, which model tier a persona gets). At nen 0.3.0 nen neither validates nor reads this file; the skills read it as data. From nen 0.4.0 `nen schema check` grows a row for it and `nen commit format` / `nen shu coverage` read it. Every value here is a policy default, not a fact about the machine.

branch.$comment: {model} is the MODEL ALIAS the actor runs on (opus, sonnet, haiku, fable), {persona} the roster persona it acts as, {descriptor} a short kebab noun phrase for the effort. Example: opus/kurapika/machinery-wave-1. `base` is the trunk breath fast-forwards, ao pulls from, and the PreToolUse hook refuses a commit or a push on.

iteration.$comment: The declared verbs rasengan runs before every commit. Hatsu is bash-and-markdown: its only mechanical check is `claude plugin validate . --strict`, declared as the `plugin` lane's `lint`. There is no build to run and no test suite to run, and both are seats in nen/contract.json saying so in the repository's own words.

tests.$comment: Hatsu ships no automated test suite; scripts/plugin_bump_check.sh is exercised by the recorded transcripts in docs/ab/plugin-bump-guard.md. tsukuyomi therefore has nothing to run here and says so rather than inventing a runner. An empty `required` is a statement, not an omission.

coverage.$comment: The ladder gyo reports against, in percent line coverage of TOUCHED files. Under `minimum` is a G5 stop, never a lowered bar. Hatsu declares no coverage verb, so gyo reports `not measurable here` against this ladder rather than a number — the ladder still ships because it is the policy every repository Hatsu drives inherits when it declares none of its own.

launch.$comment: Hatsu has no runnable application: it is a plugin read by Claude Code. amaterasu names that fact and launches nothing. A repository with launch targets names them in nen/contract.json under project.launch and selects one here.

reports.$comment: `dir` is git-ignored (.gitignore). `retain: final-only` means the per-turn and landing rikugan reports are published to the conversation and NOT written to disk; only the final post-merge report is written under `dir`. `template` names templates/<name>.html in this repository.

notifications.$comment: jutaisho's ladder, innermost first: `push` is the surface's own turn-complete signal, `os` an osascript notification, `sound` /System/Library/Sounds/<sound>.aiff through afplay. hooks/stop-bell.sh rings rungs 2 and 3 off .nen/last-stop.json; a rung absent from this list is not rung.

commits.$comment: The maintainer's ruling of 2026-09-09: `Akatsuki-Agent` is the single admitted attribution trailer, because it is the system's OWN provenance rather than a model claiming authorship. No AI attribution trailer is ever recorded. A harness that would mandate `Co-Authored-By:` is configured off (settings `includeCoAuthoredBy: false`) and the commit-msg guard refuses the trailer regardless of what any harness mandates.

monitor.$comment: en's izanagi cap and its poll interval. The cap is grammar, not a default: a watch loop with no cap does not run.

models.rule: latest alias only, never a version; subagents never on the frontier tier

cursor.note: Cursor-native only; provider models there are reserved for Bugbot

models.$comment: A tier is named, never a model version — a pinned version is a pin that rots. The orchestrator tier is the main session's; a SUBAGENT never runs on it, because the frontier tier is where the human's own conversation lives and a delegate that outranks its caller has inverted the delegation.
